sections.h2: Why is Ware County unlike the rest of south Georgia?
sections.html:
Ware County covers 908 square miles, more than any other county in Georgia, and a large block of that is wetland inside the Okefenokee Swamp and its federal refuge. Lawmakers carved it from Appling County on December 15, 1824, numbered it the state's 60th county and named it for Nicholas Ware, per Wikipedia.

Waycross is the county seat and its only incorporated city. Bickley, Ruskin, Jamestown and Telmore are unincorporated communities, so outside the city limits an address answers only to county rules. Neighbors are Bacon, Pierce, Brantley, Charlton, Clinch, Atkinson and Coffee counties, and Baker County, Florida touches the south.

Water runs three ways here. The Suwannee, St. Marys and Satilla river basins all drain parts of the county. Laura S. Walker State Park honors a local author and conservationist who promoted forest parks; the land was bought during the 1930s and deeded to Georgia in 1941.

Ware was once much bigger. Bacon, Charlton, Clinch, Coffee and Pierce counties were each formed partly from its territory. Ware County High School, Waycross Middle School, South Georgia State College and Coastal Pines Technical College are among the schools in town.

sections.h2: What do QuickFacts say about Ware County housing costs?
sections.html:
Homes here cost far less than the national average. The owner-occupied median for 2020-2024 is $109,500, roughly a third of the $332,700 U.S. figure, according to QuickFacts.

The county had 36,312 residents in 2010, 36,251 in 2020 and an estimate of 36,906 for 2025, and it holds 12,957 households. Population history is a long climb and a plateau: 8,811 in 1890, 22,957 in 1910, 37,180 in 1980 and just under 37,000 now. With so little change, most of the housing stock is existing houses, and balances left unpaid for several years can turn into recorded liens.

sections.h2: Which Ware County offices send and collect the bill?
sections.html:
The commissioner's staff bills and collects. Values come from the assessors, and the county commission and the school board each pick their own millage.

  • Tax Commissioner: 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A, Waycross, GA 31501, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502; the site header shows (912) 490-4305 and hours of 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.
  • Tax Assessors: (912) 287-4383 per the FAQ, and written appeals go to 305 Oak St., Suite 154.
  • Pay online and search parcels at warecountytax.com. If a lender escrows your tax, call the lender before paying so nothing is sent twice.
  • Deed copies: Clerk of Superior Court, 800 Church Street.

Ask the commissioner whether a City of Waycross levy shows on your county statement. The county's exemption list mentions city, county and school freezes, so city tax is part of the picture for houses inside Waycross.

sections.h2: What does a late Ware County bill cost?
sections.html:
Statements are normally mailed by September 15, and the November 15 due date follows. Manufactured homes run on a separate cycle, with bills mailed in January, payment due April 1 and a decal issued after payment.

For bills dated July 1, 2016 or later, the FAQ describes four consequences.

  • Interest at the Federal Reserve prime rate plus 3%.
  • A 5% penalty each 120 days, capped at 20% of the unpaid principal.
  • No penalty, only interest, on homesteaded property whose tax is below $500.
  • A FIFA lien recorded with the Clerk of Superior Court once more than 90 days pass.

The commissioner may also levy on the parcel. Levy sales happen on the first Tuesday of the month in the Board of Commissioners Room at 305 Oak Street, after four weeks of ads in the Waycross Journal Herald. The county gives no title guarantee, and the winning bidder has no use of the property and no rent for at least one year. The commissioner also keeps an excess funds list on the website.

sections.h2: What homestead and tax relief does Ware County offer?
sections.html:
You must own and occupy the house on January 1 to claim a homestead exemption, and you file with the Tax Assessor's office. The county's pages show both March 1 and April 1 as a filing cutoff, so confirm the date with the assessors before you apply. After approval the exemption renews itself.

  • Freeze exemptions hold the value for county, school and city operating tax at the prior-year level while you live in the home.
  • The local exemption for owners 62 and older with adjusted gross income up to $24,000 deducts as much as $20,000 from the 40% assessed value.
  • The floating exemption for owners 62 and older with household income of $30,000 or less replaces other state and county exemptions, and the county warns that it can raise a bill at first.
  • Deferral applies to owners 62 and older with gross household income of $15,000 or less.
  • Timber owners with damaged timber can use the TREES Act form from the Georgia Forestry Commission, which the commissioner's front page describes.

sections.h2: How can I challenge a Ware County valuation?
sections.html:
The window is 45 days from the date printed on the assessment notice, and arguments about taxability, value or uniformity are the ones the board will hear. A protest that the tax is simply too high is not.

Choose the Board of Equalization or an arbitrator, then continue to Superior Court by sending written notice to the assessors. Between January 1 and April 1 you can file a return naming a different value for the property.

sections.h2: What is the best way to sell a Ware County house with tax unpaid?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the commissioner, then let the closing agent pay it from your proceeds. Review the tax sale list on the county site if a levy has already been threatened, since a sale date can set the timeline.

Mobile homes carry their own April 1 bill and decal, so treat that account apart from the land. A buyer who takes the property as-is and accepts the title work can close quickly, which helps when the clock is running.

faqs.q: What date do Ware County real estate taxes come due?
faqs.a: November 15. Statements go out by about September 15, and manufactured home tax is separately due April 1.

faqs.q: Where do I find the Ware County tax office?
faqs.a: At 305 Oak Street, Suite 115A in Waycross. Mail goes to P.O. Box 1825, Waycross, GA 31502. The office opens at 8:30 a.m. and closes at 5:00 p.m. on weekdays.

faqs.q: What is the Ware County appeal deadline?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the date on the assessment notice. Send the appeal to the Board of Tax Assessors, 305 Oak St., Suite 154.

faqs.q: Does a late Ware County bill carry a penalty?
faqs.a: Yes. Interest runs at prime plus 3% and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%. Homesteaded property with tax under $500 owes interest but no penalty.

faqs.q: When are Ware County tax sales held?
faqs.a: On the first Tuesday of the month, in the Board of Commissioners Room at 305 Oak Street, after four weeks of newspaper notice. Paying the balance before the sale takes the parcel off the list.
